groups.title: Server information
groups.description: Identify a server and check whether it is ready. Players and monitoring tools can read the public checks before signing in.

groups.title: Sign-in and profiles
groups.description: Sign people in with local credentials or a TV code, select a profile and renew the session. These flows are for player apps; API keys and personal access tokens cannot replace a session on session-only routes.

groups.title: Keys and personal tokens
groups.description: Let a signed-in person create a scoped credential for a script or integration. Credential management requires a session, even when the caller already has an admin-scoped key.

groups.title: Browse and search
groups.description: Find visible libraries and titles, or build a player screen from the server’s published browse choices. Structured browse keeps filtering, ordering and access checks on the server.

groups.title: Title details and artwork
groups.description: Read title details, episode and track order, credits and images. These reads apply the viewer’s current library access and content restrictions.

groups.title: Playback sessions
groups.description: Publish the player’s real capabilities, request a presentation and report what the renderer does. Session revisions and leases keep controls and progress consistent.

groups.title: Playback queues
groups.description: Build and edit a device queue without loading all its entries. Queue revisions protect edits, and audio players can prepare the next entry before the current one ends.

groups.title: Media and subtitles
groups.description: Fetch media and subtitle resources using the URLs in a playback presentation. Grant-bearing URLs still enforce session and viewer access; clients should not construct them.

groups.title: Offline downloads
groups.description: Prepare media, transfer its companion files and retain signed permission for offline playback. Download-capable players also revalidate receipts and reconcile progress when they reconnect.

groups.title: Personal state and bulk jobs
groups.description: Read and change the current profile’s watched state, My List, favourites, history and preferences. Bulk jobs capture a selection and report progress and individual failures.

groups.title: Playlists and saved lists
groups.description: Create and edit playlists, personal collections and saved filters. Revisions and operation IDs protect list edits, and sharing remains subject to the caller’s access.

groups.title: Live TV and recordings
groups.description: Read the TV guide, play channels and manage the current viewer’s recordings. Source setup, tuner administration and storage policy belong to the server owner’s console.

groups.title: Events and notifications
groups.description: Keep open clients current with invalidation hints and a paged notification inbox. Event positions and inbox revisions are separate values.

groups.title: Title queries and scans
groups.description: Let catalogue indexes and download managers find titles and notify Portico about changed files. Scan and path-reporting writes require an owner’s credential with library scope.

groups.title: Metadata integrations
groups.description: Inspect and repair title matches or update metadata through an owner-authorized integration. These operations use library scope and keep revision checks separate from background provider work.

groups.title: Playback dashboards and controls
groups.description: Show active playback and let an authorized administrator control it. Admin scope and the administrator’s playback permission are both required.

groups.title: Webhooks
groups.description: Send signed event notifications to automation services and other integrations. An owner can manage subscriptions and inspect delivery results with an admin-scoped credential.

groups.title: AI assistants with MCP
groups.description: Connect an assistant to the server with a deliberately scoped API key or personal access token. The tool list follows both the credential’s scopes and the member’s current permissions.

operations.title: Read server information
operations.description: Returns the server ID, name, version and setup status. Use it to identify the server before signing in.

operations.title: Read the API version
operations.description: Returns the server identity and API major version and level. Use these values when checking client compatibility.

operations.title: Check whether the server is running
operations.description: Returns a small liveness response without account or dependency details. Monitoring tools can use it without credentials.

operations.title: Check database readiness
operations.description: Checks that the database responds and returns 503 when the server is not ready. Use this for an external readiness probe.

operations.title: Read the server's readiness state
operations.description: Returns the readiness flag and status, including starting or degraded states. A 503 response includes Retry-After.

operations.title: Read available features and limits
operations.description: Returns feature states and published limits for the current viewer. Use it to decide which client features to offer.

operations.title: Read available sign-in methods
operations.description: Returns the sign-in methods and policies available on this server. Read it before offering a local sign-in or pairing option.

operations.title: Sign in with local credentials
operations.description: Signs in with a username and password and returns the account snapshot and session when admission succeeds. Handle a two-factor challenge, required password change, pending device approval or account-only session before browsing.
notes: Persist a random installation ID and send X-Portico-Installation-Id and the device/app headers.
Tokenless cross-origin browser sign-in is refused; native clients can omit Origin.
Local credentials and TV codes are the documented third-party sign-in paths; third-party Portico Account assertion issuance is not provided.
API keys and personal access tokens cannot be used for this operation.

parameters.name: X-Portico-Installation-Id
parameters.description: Stable random ID for this installation, 32–128 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores.

operations.title: Complete a two-factor challenge
operations.description: Submits the challenge token and current verification code from sign-in. Success returns the sign-in result after the second factor is proven.
notes: API keys and personal access tokens cannot be used for this operation.

operations.title: Read the account and its profiles
operations.description: Returns the signed-in account snapshot and available profiles. An account-only session can use this to reach profile selection.

operations.title: Select a profile
operations.description: Selects a profile with its PIN or remembered trust token where required and returns new session credentials. Remembered trust belongs to the same installation.
notes: Save the replacement session credentials before issuing viewer requests.
API keys and personal access tokens cannot be used for this operation.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Profile ID.

operations.title: End the outgoing profile's sessions
operations.description: Revokes the outgoing profile's session families on the named installation before another profile takes over. This also ends their playback and queues on that device.
notes: Keep usable account credentials for selecting the next profile; the outgoing families are revoked.
API keys and personal access tokens cannot be used for this operation.

operations.title: Change the local account password
operations.description: Changes the password after proving the current password and any required second factor. Use it to complete a required password change, then sign in again because existing sessions end.
notes: API keys and personal access tokens cannot be used for this operation.

operations.title: Renew a session
operations.description: Exchanges the refresh token for a new session envelope bound to the installation. Save both tokens atomically and retry a lost response with the same refresh token, installation ID and request ID.
notes: Store refresh tokens privately and serialize refreshes within the app. Reusing a predecessor outside an exact retry can revoke its session family.
API keys and personal access tokens cannot be used for this operation.

operations.title: Read the current viewer
operations.description: Returns the authenticated viewer's identity and permissions. Use it after profile selection to establish whose state the app is showing.

operations.title: Read a profile picture
operations.description: Returns a profile's avatar image subject to access checks. Use the returned avatar URL when displaying the profile picker.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Profile ID from the account’s profile list.

parameters.name: v
parameters.description: Avatar version from the returned URL.

operations.title: Sign out this session
operations.description: Revokes the entire current session family, including its playback access. It accepts an authentic expired or retired family token and takes no query or body.
notes: API keys and personal access tokens cannot be used for this operation.

operations.title: Request a TV sign-in code
operations.description: Creates a pairing attempt and returns the display code, verification URLs, expiry and polling interval. Keep deviceCode private and show the returned verification address.
notes: Persist a random installation ID and send X-Portico-Installation-Id and the device/app headers.
Tokenless cross-origin browser sign-in is refused; native clients can omit Origin.
API keys and personal access tokens cannot be used for this operation.

operations.title: Review a TV sign-in request
operations.description: Looks up a user code so the signed-in viewer can inspect the waiting device before deciding. This step does not approve it.
notes: API keys and personal access tokens cannot be used for this operation.

operations.title: Approve or deny a TV sign-in
operations.description: Records the signed-in viewer's decision for a user code and returns 204. An approved device receives the approver's identity and role, including owner authority when the owner approves.
notes: Approval grants the approver’s identity and role to the waiting device.
API keys and personal access tokens cannot be used for this operation.

operations.title: Collect the TV session
operations.description: Polls a pairing attempt with its secret device code and returns the session envelope after approval. Honour the polling interval and Retry-After for authorization_pending or slow_down, and stop on denial or expiry.
notes: API keys and personal access tokens cannot be used for this operation.

operations.title: Cancel a TV sign-in request
operations.description: Cancels an unused pairing attempt with its device code. Call it when the viewer leaves the waiting screen.
notes: API keys and personal access tokens cannot be used for this operation.

operations.title: Read credential options and limits
operations.description: Returns the available scopes, credential limits and whether members may create personal tokens. Read this before presenting a credential form.
notes: API keys and personal access tokens cannot be used for this operation.

operations.title: List your personal access tokens
operations.description: Lists the current member's tokens with hints, usage and lifecycle state. Stored secrets cannot be read back.
notes: API keys and personal access tokens cannot be used for this operation.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page or window size within this operation’s published bounds.

operations.title: Create a personal access token
operations.description: Creates a token for the signed-in member with the requested scopes and optional expiry. The operation ID prevents duplicate creation, but a replay does not return the secret again.
notes: Save the secret from the first response; it is not returned on an idempotent replay.
API keys and personal access tokens cannot be used for this operation.

operations.title: Revoke a personal access token
operations.description: Revokes one of the current member's tokens and takes effect on its next request. Revocation is safe to repeat.
notes: API keys and personal access tokens cannot be used for this operation.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Personal access token ID.

operations.title: List server API keys
operations.description: Lets the owner list integration keys, including their scopes, usage and state. The list shows secret hints rather than full secrets.
notes: API keys and personal access tokens cannot be used for this operation.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Continuation returned by the previous page; send it unchanged with the same query.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page or window size within this operation’s published bounds.

operations.title: Create an API key
operations.description: Lets a signed-in owner create a scoped integration key with an optional expiry. Save the secret from the first successful response; replaying the operation ID does not reveal it again.
notes: Save the secret from the first response; it is not returned on an idempotent replay.
API keys and personal access tokens cannot be used for this operation.

operations.title: Revoke an API key
operations.description: Lets a signed-in owner revoke an integration key. The key stops working on its next request and the revocation is safe to repeat.
notes: API keys and personal access tokens cannot be used for this operation.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: API key ID.

operations.description: Returns configured webhooks and the event types available for subscriptions. Secrets are represented by hints.

operations.title: Create a webhook
operations.description: Adds a destination and event subscription and returns its signing secret once. URLs may use HTTP or HTTPS, including a private network address, but cannot contain a username or password.
notes: Keep the signing secret privately; it is shown only when issued or replaced.
Requires the owner; an API key or personal token also needs admin scope.

operations.title: Read a webhook
operations.description: Returns one webhook's configuration, revision and delivery state. Read it before changing a subscription.
notes: Requires the owner; an API key or personal token also needs admin scope.

operations.description: Changes the destination, events or enabled state using expectedRevision. Setting rotateSecret returns the replacement signing secret once; disabling a webhook abandons queued deliveries.
notes: Keep the signing secret privately; it is shown only when issued or replaced.
Requires the owner; an API key or personal token also needs admin scope.

operations.description: Returns a paged delivery log, newest first, with attempt counts and HTTP results. Event IDs stay the same across retries so receivers can ignore duplicate deliveries.

operations.title: Call the MCP server
operations.description: Accepts MCP JSON-RPC over stateless Streamable HTTP, with JSON responses and no session ID to retain. Use initialize, tools/list and tools/call with an API key or personal token; signed-in app sessions are refused.
notes: Use an API key or personal access token; the route’s open scope label does not mean unauthenticated MCP access.
POST supports initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call and notifications. GET returns 405; there is no server event stream.
Supported protocol versions: 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05. Tools are filtered by scope, role and configured features.
